title: Awesome Terminal — iTerm2 + Zsh + Oh My Zsh + Amazon Q
excerpt: Optimize your terminal with iTerm2, Zsh, Oh My Zsh, and Amazon Q - a guide to installation, theme customization, plugins, and configuration for an enhanced command-line experience.
content:
## Install iTerm2

### Download

https://iterm2.com/downloads.html

### Custom Theme

https://draculatheme.com/iterm

## Install Oh My Zsh

Reference: https://ohmyz.sh/#install

```bash
sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/master/tools/install.sh)"
```

## Install Oh My Zsh Theme

Reference: https://github.com/gowtham/gowthamdev.zsh-theme

```bash
git clone git@github.com:gowtham/gowthamdev.zsh-theme.git ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-~/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/themes/gowthamdev.zsh-theme
```

**Activate the theme**

```bash title="~/.zshrc"
ZSH_THEME="gowthamdev.zsh-theme/gowtham"
```

## Install Oh My Zsh Plugins

### zsh-z

Reference: https://github.com/agkozak/zsh-z#installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/agkozak/zsh-z $ZSH_CUSTOM/plugins/zsh-z
```

### zsh-syntax-highlighting

Reference: https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting/blob/master/INSTALL.md

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting.git ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-~/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting
```

### zsh-autosuggestions

Reference: https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions/blob/master/INSTALL.md

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-~/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions
```

### Activate plugins

```bash title="~/.zshrc"
plugins=(git zsh-z zsh-syntax-highlighting zsh-autosuggestions)
```

## User Configuration

```bash title="~/.zshrc"
# Language environment
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8

# Alias
alias workspace-on-mac="cd ~/Workspace"

# Homebrew
export HOMEBREW_EDITOR="/usr/bin/nano"
```

## Install Amazon Q for command line

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/command-line-installing.html

title: Welcome to gowthamdev.com
excerpt: A minimal portfolio, component registry, and blog to showcase my work as a Design Engineer.
content:
## Tech Stack

- Next.js 15
- Tailwind CSS v4
- shadcn/ui

## Featured

- Clean & modern design
- Light & Dark theme support
- vCard integration
- SEO optimization: [JSON-LD schema](https://json-ld.org), sitemap, robots
- AI-friendly [/llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org)
- Spam-protected email
- Installable PWA

## Blog

- MDX & Markdown support
- Access markdown by adding `.md` to URLs, e.g. `/blog/welcome.md`
- Syntax Highlighting for better readability
- RSS Feed for easy content distribution
- Dynamic OG Images for rich previews

## Component Registry

Easily build and distribute your own components, hooks, and pages using a custom registry powered by the [shadcn CLI](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli).

Each component is well-documented through the Blog, featuring:

- **Live Preview**: Interactive component demos
- **Code Snippets**: Readable and copyable examples
- **Beautiful Code Blocks**: Styled for clarity and dark mode
- **Command Blocks**: One-click copy for quick install commands (`pnpm`, `npm`, `yarn`, `bun`)

## License

Licensed under the [MIT license](https://github.com/gowtham/gowthamdev.com/blob/main/LICENSE).

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/gowtham/gowthamdev.com). You're free to use my code! Just make sure to remove all my personal information before publishing your website. It's awesome to see my code being useful to someone!

title: React Wheel Picker joins Vercel Open Source Program!
content:
I'm thrilled to share that React Wheel Picker has been selected to join the Vercel Open Source Program: Summer cohort!

React Wheel Picker is a lightweight, customizable, and touch-friendly picker component for React — built to deliver a smooth, native-like scrolling experience across modern browsers. It started as a side project, and it's been amazing to see it grow with the help of open source contributors and feedback from users.

Being part of Vercel OSS Program means the project will receive $300/month in infrastructure credits for the next 12 months, along with support from the developer community. I'm incredibly grateful for Vercel's support — it's a big motivation to keep improving the project and pushing it forward.

If you're curious, feel free to explore the demo or dive into the code:

Live Demo: https://react-wheel-picker.gowthamdev.com
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/gowtham/react-wheel-picker
excerpt: Excited to share that my open source project is now officially supported by Vercel!
